content:
Cybersecurity firm Jamf has discovered a fake Mac installer disguised as the Zoom video conferencing software, which uses a clever technique to bypass Apple's Gatekeeper protection mechanism designed to prevent malware.

The malware does indeed install Zoom, but it also plants an information-stealing program that extracts user data and sends it to the attacker's server…

Normally, if you try to install a Mac application that has not been notarised by Apple, macOS will refuse to open it. Although there are ways to bypass this restriction, the process is quite cumbersome, and attackers must find a way to convince users to perform the necessary steps.

Jamf has named this malware CloudSyncD. The threat actors behind it found a clever way to make the above operation appear more legitimate. The software's installation dropper contains a background image with operating instructions, as shown in the image above.

You have to admire their creativity.

Once the malware is installed, it can log user input and send the data to the attackers as frequently as every eight seconds.

As always, you should only install Mac applications from the official Mac App Store or from a developer website you trust.
